messages:
alexa: heads-up — saw a pager come through from incident-bot about a regional latency spike hitting prod-nyc. :rotating_light: looks customer-facing; metrics show elevated p50/p95 on text-gen endpoints

incident-bot: [PAGER] Severity: P2 — Latency spike detected on /v1/generate (prod-nyc). Affected traffic: 18%. Thresholds crossed: p95 > 1.2s for 5m. Links: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/3054321987

oncall-rotation-bot: Current on-call: primary=mike, secondary=sanjay, shadow=lee. Primary oncall since 2026-03-14 08:00 UTC.

mike: i'm on it, jumping in. grabbing logs and runbook.

alexa: mike — quick context: customer-impacting if >15% requests degrade. we should treat as customer visible and follow escalation matrix in the runbook.

mike: confirmed. initial triage: tailing runtime logs shows backlog on gpu-pool-3, `queue_depth` spiking to 120. error rate is stable. looks like serving throughput degraded, not model errors.

lee: useful runbook bits: see runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/serving-latency — check pool health, OOMs, kernel errors, and router fallback rates. also check cache hit ratios.

mike: running `kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=gpu-pool-3 -o wide` — a couple pods are in CrashLoopBackOff. logs show `failed to allocate kv-cache: out of memory` followed by driver resets. pasted snippets:

```
[2026-03-14T08:12:21Z] inference-runtime gpu-3-2: ERROR failed to allocate kv-cache: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-14T08:12:22Z] inference-runtime gpu-3-2: WARN fallback to small-kv-profile for new sessions
```

sanjay: if pods crash we need to avoid mass restart → that can cause cascading cold starts and amplify latency. recommended immediate action: scale up spare pool capacity (if available) or activate fallback routing to dedicated-light models.

alexa: escalation rule reminder — page secondary after 10m if primary still working but impact persists. escalate to eng-sre lead (oncall pager) at 30m. if customer SLA risk, notify CSM.

mike: scaling attempt: `kubectl scale deployment gpu-pool-3 --replicas=6` — cluster autoscaler slow; provisioning 1 GPU node pending. meanwhile toggled routing: bumped fallback-policy to route 20% of traffic to gpu-pool-1 (warm spare). command: `redwoodctl route-set --service text-gen --policy fallback:20% --from=pools:gpu-pool-3 to=pools:gpu-pool-1`

incident-bot: Action logged: manual route change by mike. Applied fallback 20% -> gpu-pool-1. Expected mitigation window: 2-3m.

lee: good. monitor for increased latency on gpu-pool-1 (it might have different kernel selection causing slight regression). Also watch for tokenization failures when routing.

mike: initial metric delta: affected traffic down to 9% in 3m. p95 trending down to 0.9s. keeping an eye.

alexa: mike — given you manually intervened and mitigation is effective, no need to page sanjay immediately. but mark this thread and do a structured handoff at the top of next hour in case residual issues surface.

mike: agreed. i'll continue monitoring for 30m and then hand off status with checklist: what, why, actions taken, rollback plan.

sanjay: if this resurfaces after handoff, page me immediately (pager priority). for clarity: paging sequence = primary -> 10m escalate to secondary -> 30m escalate to eng-sre lead -> 60m exec notif if >5 customer incidents.

alexa: also capture customer impact: CSM note draft: `Latency spike in NYC impacted ~18% of text-gen requests; mitigation applied via routing to warm spare; residual impact <10%; no data loss; tracking improvements`. Put in incident timeline and link when done.

mike: putting timeline in ops doc now: https://docs.internal/incidents/3054321987 — I'm adding bullet list and runbook pointers.

incident-bot: Reminder scheduled: auto-check in at +10m, +30m, +60m.

lee: small operational pointer — if we see more `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` across pools, it's likely a driver mismatch after last kernel update. flag to infra-releases and pause the rollout.

mike: thanks — will watch. current plan: continue monitoring, avoid mass pod recycle, keep fallback routing until cluster capacity stabilizes, and prepare a brief handoff in 25m.

alexa: thanks team. mike — please post final handoff here with `Handoff:` header and include `primary/secondary/what to watch/rollback` before you leave shift. :raised_hands:

mike: Handoff: primary=mike, secondary=sanjay. What to watch: p95 for /v1/generate in prod-nyc, pool queue_depth, CrashLoopBackOff count, autoscaler events. Actions taken: fallback routing 20%->gpu-pool-1, scaled gpu-pool-3 to 6 replicas, created ops doc. Rollback plan: revert routing with `redwoodctl route-set --service text-gen --policy fallback:0%` after p95 stable for 15m, and drain any newly provisioned nodes if not needed. Contact points: sanjay (pager), lee (infra).

sanjay: acknowledged. i'll take over if needed and will escalate per the paging sequence. thanks for tidy handoff.

incident-bot: Thread closed for updates by auto-check after +60m unless reactivated.
